args.reason: The old decision's own rationale (fewer than 20 issues per run, simple atomic writes) is contradicted by current facts: runs admit 200+ issues and a concurrency executor now writes issues in parallel. The new design addresses two concrete failure modes the old one did not consider (single-lock contention, one corrupt byte losing all run state), keeps the same directory root, and adds an index file for discovery. The supersession argument holds. Residual implementation risk to watch: the index file and per-issue files can disagree after a partial write, so readers should tolerate an index entry with no file and vice versa.
